mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-46.0 to -40.6), indicating self-reinforcing recovery momentum as consumer confidence and store reopenings compound; this trend continues, lifting mean RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks above the last 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from -46.0 to -40.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the prior three-week improving streak.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (49.0 to 27.3, a 21.7 point fall) signals that outdoor-recreation substitution is weakening, pushing displaced leisure activity back toward retail and recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 49.0 to 27.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks following a PARKS drop exceeding 15 points, or falls alongside continued PARKS decline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain flat week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL drifts downward, the joint signal indicates a stable commuting baseline combined with marginally less home-confinement, together enabling incremental growth in discretionary retail trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each change less than 3 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL declines
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES varied by less than 2 points across the last three weeks while RESIDENTIAL fell from 15.1 to 13.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay flat and RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state reopening regime with no detectable new restrictions (WORKPLACES and TRANSIT essentially unchanged for three weeks), RETAIL_REC recovery continues but decelerates, since the week-on-week gains are already shrinking (1.6, 3.3, 0.5 points), producing a smaller but still positive 4-week shift.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held near -46 and TRANSIT near -53 to -55 for all four weeks
fact:RETAIL_REC week-on-week gains shrank from 3.3 to 0.5 points
regime_hint: steady-state reopening plateau, no new restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC turns flat or negative over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining unchanged, or the deceleration reverses into renewed acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-August marks the seasonal transition toward end-of-summer and back-to-school activity, historically shifting household trips from outdoor parks toward indoor retail and recreation venues as families prepare for the school year, raising RETAIL_REC over the following 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2020-08-15, within the seasonal back-to-school window
regime_hint: seasonal transition (late summer to early fall)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even as PARKS mobility continues to decline into early fall.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily over three weeks (15.1 to 13.0), indicating households are spending incrementally less time at home; this reduction in home-confinement directly frees time for near-term retail and recreation trips within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 15.1 to 13.0 over the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following continued RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility deteriorates sharply below current levels, it would signal a shift toward essential-only trip behavior consistent with renewed public-health caution or policy tightening, which would suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -25 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has drifted from -19.1 to -20.4 over the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or stays flat even after GROCERY_PHARM falls below -25, invalidating the essential-only substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained deeply suppressed near -53 to -56 for all four weeks with no sign of recovery, acting as a structural ceiling on commute-linked and transit-dependent retail trips; prolonged transit suppression caps RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks even if other indicators improve.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 for 4 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged from -55.6 to -53.3 with no improving trend across all four weeks
